answers.falsifier: git check-attr eol reads lf for a .py, a .md and a .txt path under the repo's .gitattributes ; the pin leaves the .cmd crlf and the existing json/sh pins as they were
answers.how: Add `*.py text eol=lf`, `*.md text eol=lf` and `*.txt text eol=lf` to .gitattributes beside the json and sh pins, with a why-comment. Run git add --renormalize on tracked files in the build commit. Proof: copy the repo's real .gitattributes into a scratch git repo and read git check-attr eol for a .py, a .md and a .txt path (eol: lf), and for a .cmd path (crlf, untouched). The fingerprint equality is the measured why, kept in the ticket, not re-asserted by the proof.
answers.title: source files are LF on every box, so a seal's fingerprint means the same bytes everywhere
answers.traces_to: Law 3: a fingerprint is a measurement and has to mean the same bytes on every box; Law 4: the line ending is enforced by git's attributes, not by a reader remembering.
answers.what: cairn/.gitattributes pins *.py, *.md and *.txt to eol=lf, so a checkout holds the same bytes on every box and a seal's fingerprint means the same bytes everywhere; git add --renormalize in the build commit, which is empty because the blobs are already LF.
